raw_text: {"schema_version":"chat_response_v1","response_type":"answer","answer_text":"DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides in the 5' to 3' direction, and it needs a free 3'-OH group to extend from [ev_006]. Because the two template strands are antiparallel, one new strand can be extended continuously toward the replication fork; this is the leading strand [ev_001] [ev_007]. The other new strand is synthesized away from the replication fork in short pieces called Okazaki fragments, and each fragment needs its own RNA primer to start synthesis; this is the lagging strand [ev_001] [ev_007]. The overall direction of the lagging strand is 3' to 5', and that of the leading strand is 5' to 3' [ev_002]. RNA primers are replaced by DNA as synthesis proceeds: DNA pol I removes the primers by its exonuclease activity, uses the DNA behind the RNA as its own primer, and fills the gaps with DNA nucleotides [ev_002].
